subject: Whether the transport and plug-in menu could be driven in any language but Korean and English
question: Was the two-language shape an oversight in a few call sites, or the shape of the API?

reverify.expected: every AX comparison outside a LabelSet is on a string Apple does not translate
reverify.cost: ~40s; reads committed digest sets and the Swift tree

method: Swept every string literal compared against a variable this tree assigns from an accessibility accessor, kept the ones Apple ships AND translates, then read the control-bar and plug-in-menu call sites.

observations.what: AX comparisons outside a LabelSet on a string Apple translates, before
of those that were internal identifiers, not AX readings
control-bar controls reachable before, by language
observations.detail: the table was (korean:, english:) and the finder took two String parameters

observations.what: locales Count In is reachable in after deriving it
locales the plug-in menu's Audio Units is reachable in
the plug-in menu category Apple ships no key for, read off a live menu
observations.note: English and Korean are what the product had; the other eight locales are unmeasured.

conclusion: It was the shape of the API. `findControlBarCheckbox` took `named koreanName: String, englishName: String?`, so a German or Chinese Logic could not be matched at all -- there was nowhere to put the label, and `transport.stop` looked for 재생 and Play against a checkbox titled Wiedergabe. The control bar now takes a LabelSet and nothing else, so two-language matching is not expressible. Count In was derived from Apple's own data in 10 locales, where the table had carried 2. Audio Units likewise. Utility could not be derived -- Apple ships no key for it -- so it is carried as a measured LabelSet with one locale and nine gaps that are now countable instead of hidden in a hard-coded ||.
limits: Derived values are Apple's bytes, not readings from a running Logic in those locales. That a German Logic titles the checkbox `Einzählen` follows from the table, and nobody has driven one.
Utility carries Korean only. The other nine locales are unmeasured and the LabelSet says so.
The sweep covers `Sources/` and `Scripts/livekit/`. A comparison written in a language other than Swift was not examined.
It finds comparisons against variables assigned from an accessor IN THE SAME FILE. A reading passed through two files is invisible to it.

canon.used_for: the control-bar count-in checkbox, whose nine other locales this record derives
the plug-in menu category the menu is recognised by
